prerequisites: Basic formulation and nomenclature of organic and inorganic compounds.
Balancing chemical equations and simple stoichiometric calculations.
Ways to express solution concentrations and associated stoichiometric calculations.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Organization Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Ability to understand and apply the principles of basic knowledge of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.
Consolidate knowledge of the fundamentals of chemical terminology, nomenclature, conventions and units.
Relate macroscopic properties with those of the constituent atoms and molecules of matter.
Identify the characteristics of different states of aggregation.
Describe the types of chemical reactions and their main associated characteristics.
Solve quantitative and qualitative problems according to previously developed models.
Apply the principles of thermodynamics and its applications in Chemistry.
Recognize and value chemical processes in daily life.
Relate Chemistry to other disciplines.
Develop critical reasoning.
Learn autonomously.
Acquire the ability to evaluate, interpret and synthesize chemical information.
Work in a team.
Demonstrate and use basic knowledge of Chemistry fluently.
Formulate and solve basic problems in the field of Chemistry.
Correctly use the basic terminology employed in the field of chemistry, expressing ideas with precision, being able to establish relationships between different concepts.
Apply the techniques used in a basic chemistry laboratory, including the necessary calculations and expressing the results appropriately.
Prepare and correctly present reports, both orally and in writing, corresponding to the laboratory practices carried out in the Chemistry course.

syllabus_topics: Object of Chemistry and its relationship with other sciences.
Meaning of chemical formulas and chemical nomenclature.
Formulation and nomenclature of simple inorganic and organic compounds.
Amount of substance, mole and Avogadro's number.
General properties of the states of matter.
Ways to express the concentration of solutions.
First law of Thermodynamics: basic concepts.
Entropy and the second and third laws of Thermodynamics.
Control of reaction rate: influence of concentration and temperature.
Chemical equilibrium in a reaction between gases.
Control of chemical equilibrium and Le Châtelier's principle.
pH and dissociation constants of acids and bases.
Standard reduction potentials and electrochemical series.
Safety and Basic Laboratory Operations: Toxicity of chemical substances. Pictograms and safety information sheets. Measurement of masses and volumes. Preparation of solutions.
Molecular Models: Lewis structures. Determination of formal charges. Resonance.
Qualitative Studies of Chemical Reactions: Observation of reaction heats. Factors influencing reaction rate. Shifting chemical equilibrium. Chemical reactions in ion separation and identification.
Calorimetry and Reaction Enthalpies: Heat capacity and calorimeter constant. Determination of calorimetric curves.
Determination of Kinetic Laws: Empirical kinetic laws. Method of initial rates.
Quantitative Chemical Analysis: Volumetric determinations with chemical and/or instrumental indicator.
Synthesis of Chemical Compounds: Reaction conditions. Product purification and yield determination.
Redox Processes and Electrochemical Cells: Redox properties of metals. Measurement of the electromotive force of electrochemical cells.
Separation Operations: Liquid-liquid extraction. Separation of binary mixtures.
Conductivity of Electrolyte Solutions: Classification of electrolytes. Molar conductivity.
assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in each assessable aspect (P1, P2, PA, TG, PL follow-up, PL written test). The weighted sum of the assessable aspects must be equal to or greater than 5 out of 10 to pass. If a student does not achieve a minimum of 4 in P1 or does not attend, the final exam (E Final) will account for 60% of the grade, with a minimum of 4 required. For extraordinary calls, a minimum of 5 out of 10 is required for both the global exam (E Final) and the average of the laboratory practices, otherwise the weighted formula will not be applied.
